# Node creation routes and the decision model

12 routes. All are **defined**; none is implemented in this phase.

| Route | Use when | Runtimes | Portability | Trust | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `no-code-api` | a REST API wrapped by configuration alone | `js-compat` | `network-required` | `verified` | defined |
| `declarative` | n8n's declarative style: routing described as data | `js-compat`, `wasm` | `network-required` | `verified` | defined |
| `openapi` | generate a node from an OpenAPI/Swagger document | `js-compat`, `wasm` | `network-required` | `verified` | defined |
| `visual-builder` | a node assembled in a UI by a non-programmer | `js-compat` | `portable` | `verified` | defined |
| `transform-formula` | pure data transformation via an expression | `js-compat`, `wasm`, `rust-native` | `portable` | `verified` | defined |
| `workflow-as-node` | an existing workflow reused as a single node | `js-compat` | `portable` | `core` | defined |
| `javascript` | arbitrary logic, and the entire existing n8n ecosystem | `js-compat` | `portable` | `community` | supported-today |
| `python` | data/ML work where the Python ecosystem is decisive | `remote-worker` | `process-required` | `community` | defined |
| `wasm` | portable, sandboxed compute | `wasm` | `portable` | `community` | defined |
| `rust` | hot paths where CPU/memory cost is material | `rust-native` | `native-required` | `core` | defined-not-implemented |
| `remote` | execution that cannot or should not happen on this device | `remote-worker` | `remote-capable` | `verified` | defined |
| `community` | reuse what the n8n ecosystem already has | `js-compat` | `portable` | `community` | supported-today |

## Decision rules (first match wins)

| Rule | When | Prefer | Because |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D1` | an existing community node already does it | `community` | zero implementation and zero maintenance beat any rewrite |
| `D2` | it is a REST API wrapper | `no-code-api or declarative` | no code means no attack surface and no upgrade cost |
| `D3` | an OpenAPI document exists | `openapi` | regeneration is cheaper than maintenance |
| `D4` | it is a pure, hot, deterministic transform | `rust or wasm` | this is where native speed is actually material |
| `D5` | portability or sandboxing matters more than peak speed | `wasm` | one prebuilt artifact runs everywhere, isolated |
| `D6` | the device is constrained and the work is heavy | `remote` | the catalog should not shrink on a phone |
| `D7` | the Python ecosystem is the reason it exists | `python` | rewriting discards the only justification |
| `D8` | nothing above applies | `javascript` | it is the ecosystem default and always compatible |

Executable: `decideCreationRoute(facts)` in `src/lego/foundation.mjs` — it returns the rule that fired, so a recommendation is always explainable.

## Rust policy

- must ship prebuilt per platform — never require a compiler on a user device
- must implement the SAME Node Contract, with the same identity and error codes
- must not break JS or community-node compatibility
- must be replaceable back to JS if it regresses

Guard: `isRustJustified(facts)`. Tie-break: When two routes score equally, choose the one with the lower total lifecycle cost: maintenance + upgrade + scale-out, not implementation time.

## Community-node compatibility

- Existing n8n community nodes keep loading. The compatibility runtime is the default, not a fallback.
- Node identity (`type` + `typeVersion`) never changes because of a migration, a runtime change or a reimplementation. A saved workflow that referenced a node must keep resolving it.
- The migration path is one-directional and optional: JS node -> Node Contract descriptor -> compatibility runtime -> (much later, only if justified) an alternative implementation behind the same contract.
- A node author is never required to adopt the Node Contract. Adoption buys better metadata, capability declarations and portability information; it is not a condition of running.
- No community node is ever rewritten in Rust in order to keep working. Rust is an optional additional implementation, never a requirement.
- A node whose package fails verification is quarantined, never silently disabled and never deleted before the cause is recorded.
